questions.enonce_markdown:
PERT chart is a tool used in project management. Below is the PERT chart of a project.

![fig-1](gce-al-ict-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_8_fig_1.png)

(a) State the full meaning of the acronym PERT. (1 mark)

(b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using PERT charts. (2 marks)

(c) Calculate the critical path of the project. (3 marks)

(d) State the slack time of each of the tasks B, F, and E. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) PERT (1 mark).** **Program Evaluation and Review Technique**.

**(b) One advantage and one disadvantage (2 marks)**

- *Advantage:* it **shows clearly the order and the dependencies of the tasks** and so allows the project manager to find the **critical path** and the shortest time in which the project can be completed (it also helps to plan resources and to see which tasks can be delayed).
- *Disadvantage:* it is **complicated and time-consuming to draw and to update for a big project**, and the time estimates are only guesses, so the results may be unreliable.

**(c) Critical path (3 marks)**

The numbers on the arrows are the durations (the unit is not printed). A forward pass gives the **earliest time** of each task (the largest total of the paths reaching it):

- A = 0
- B = 0 + 3 = 3
- C = the larger of (A to C) 0 + 2 = 2 and (B to C) 3 + 1 = 4, so C = **4**
- D = 0 + 6 = 6
- G = 3 + 3 = 6
- F = 4 + 2 = 6
- E = 4 + 4 = 8
- H = the largest of F + 3 = 9, E + 1 = 9 and D + 2 = 8, so H = **9**
- I = the larger of G + 4 = 10 and H + 2 = 11, so I = **11**

The project takes **11 time units**. The paths and their lengths are:

| Path | Length |
|---|---|
| A - B - C - F - H - I | 3 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 2 = **11** |
| A - B - C - E - H - I | 3 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 2 = **11** |
| A - B - G - I | 3 + 3 + 4 = 10 |
| A - D - H - I | 6 + 2 + 2 = 10 |
| A - C - F - H - I | 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 9 |
| A - C - E - H - I | 2 + 4 + 1 + 2 = 9 |

**The critical path is A - B - C - F - H - I (length 11); the path A - B - C - E - H - I, also of length 11, is critical too.** (Both are the longest paths.)

**(d) Slack time of B, F and E (2 marks)**

The slack of a task is the **latest time minus the earliest time**. A backward pass from I = 11 gives the latest times: H = 11 - 2 = 9; F = 9 - 3 = 6; E = 9 - 1 = 8; C = the smaller of F - 2 = 4 and E - 4 = 4, so C = 4; G = 11 - 4 = 7; B = the smaller of G - 3 = 4 and C - 1 = 3, so B = 3.

| Task | Earliest | Latest | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | 3 | 3 | **0** |
| F | 6 | 6 | **0** |
| E | 8 | 8 | **0** |

**The slack time of B, F and E is 0 for each**, because all three lie on a critical path: any delay in them delays the whole project. (For comparison, the slack of G is 7 - 6 = 1 and that of D is 7 - 6 = 1.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain TWO ways you can restrict access to a database. (2 marks)

(b) Describe two elements that are used to collect data in a database. (2 marks)

(c) Give TWO advantages of database over flat file system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Two ways to restrict access to a database (2 marks)**

1. **User names (IDs) and passwords (authentication):** only the people who give a valid user name and password can open the database; biometric identification can be used in the same way.
2. **Access rights (privileges) and views:** each user or group of users receives only the permissions needed, for example read-only access, or the right to add or change data but not to delete, and a **view** shows each user only the tables or fields that concern him or her.

(Other accepted ways: encryption of the data, physical protection of the server, firewall.)

**(b) Two elements used to collect data (2 marks)**

1. **Forms (data-entry forms):** screens with labelled boxes (fields) in which the user types or selects the data one record at a time; validation rules, drop-down lists and check boxes reduce the errors.
2. **Tables (fields and records):** data can be entered directly in the datasheet view of a table, where each column is a field and each row a record; the data type and the validation rule of each field control what can be entered.

**(c) Two advantages of a database over a flat-file system (2 marks)**

1. **Less data redundancy and better consistency:** the data are stored once in related tables, so there is no duplication and no conflicting copies, unlike a flat file where the same data are repeated in every record.
2. **Easier and faster searching, sharing and security:** queries and reports can be made quickly on several tables; many users can use the same data at the same time, and access rights can be set for each user. (Also: data integrity, data independence, easier back-up and recovery.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
The price of a food item is gotten by first measuring them in bags and then multiplying the number of bags by a unit amount of 4600Frs.

(a) Write a pseudocode for the above process. (2 marks)

(b) Identify and justify the type of control structure used in your pseudocode. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Pseudocode (2 marks)**

```text
BEGIN
    SET UnitPrice <- 4600          // price of one bag, in Frs
    INPUT NumberOfBags             // measured number of bags
    SET TotalPrice <- NumberOfBags * UnitPrice
    OUTPUT TotalPrice
END
```

Check (Python translation executed): 3 bags give 13800 Frs, 10 bags give 46000 Frs, 0 bag gives 0 Frs.

**(b) Control structure (1 mark).** The control structure is **sequence**: the statements (input, calculation, output) are executed **one after the other in the order in which they are written**. There is no condition to test (no selection) and nothing to repeat (no iteration).
